metadata.title: Inertia: The Puck That Never Stops
metadata.register: formal, undergrad/grad audience, no casual narration, no doodle asides
metadata.branding: none — unbranded, book content only, no channel/logo/handle

beats.narration_text: Push a puck and it always slides to a stop. But what if nothing was actually slowing it down?
beats.new_visual_element: Short-only question card: the driving question appears centered on screen in ink text with a crimson underline, posed before any explanation begins.
beats.accumulated_scene_state: question card faded out, blank cream background

beats.narration_text: Push a puck, and it slides, then it stops. Common sense says that is simply what moving things do.
beats.new_visual_element: A puck on a tabletop. A crimson arrow labeled PUSH taps it from the left. The puck slides right and gradually decelerates to a stop about a third of the way across the table.
beats.accumulated_scene_state: puck at rest partway across the table

beats.narration_text: But something was touching it the entire time. Friction acts backward against its motion, quietly stealing away its speed.
beats.new_visual_element: A teal arrow appears beneath the puck, pointing backward against its direction of travel, labeled FRICTION. It fades as the puck slows and disappears once the puck is at rest.
beats.accumulated_scene_state: puck at rest, friction arrow faded out

beats.narration_text: Now turn on the air, lifting the puck just off the surface. Friction disappears, and with it, the only thing that was ever slowing the puck down. It glides at a constant speed, never losing any.
beats.new_visual_element: Small slate arrows appear across the table, representing air jets. The puck is pushed again with the same crimson arrow. This time the teal friction arrow flashes once and vanishes. The puck glides right at constant speed all the way across the table.
beats.accumulated_scene_state: puck gliding at constant speed near the right edge of the table, no friction arrow present

beats.narration_text: This is Newton's first law. When the net force on an object is zero, its velocity stays exactly constant, forever. No force is required to keep something moving, only to change how it moves.
beats.new_visual_element: The puck glides across the table again at constant speed. Above it, a gold-highlighted two-line statement reads: net force equals zero. velocity equals constant.
beats.accumulated_scene_state: puck gliding at constant speed, gold-highlighted law statement above it

beats.narration_text: The puck was never trying to stop. All along, it was simply trying to keep going.
beats.new_visual_element: The puck holds mid-table, labeled INERTIA beside it. A gold-highlighted line of text beneath reads: nothing stops it, because nothing is pushing it to stop.
beats.accumulated_scene_state: final held frame: puck labeled INERTIA, gold-highlighted punchline text beneath
